Background checks, push from TrueNAS, what to notify about
Notifications are blocked: tap to allow them

TrueCtrl can check your TrueNAS in the background and tell you when something needs attention. Push through the ntfy app and your own ntfy server adds instant notifications for every TrueNAS alert, with the background check as a fallback.
Notifications are turned off for TrueCtrl.
Looks at every saved server and notifies about new problems

Android runs background checks at most every 15 minutes, and can delay them to save battery. Each check opens its own short, read-only connection. Server unreachable and pool usage above your warning level can only come from these checks, so keep them on even with push.

ntfy temporarily unavailable: it can\'t reach your ntfy server right now. The push address stays the same, and alerts arrive again once the server is back.

Adds a \"TrueCtrl\" alert service on TrueNAS that sends alerts of your chosen level to this push address
Set it up in TrueNAS yourself

TrueCtrl can do this for you when your user has the Alert Write role. Otherwise, in the TrueNAS web UI:
1. Open System › Alert Settings and add an alert service.
2. Name: TrueCtrl. Type: Slack. Webhook URL: the push address above (tap it to copy).
3. Level: Warning, then Send Test Alert and Save.
TrueNAS has no ntfy type, but its Slack type sends each alert as a small JSON message that TrueCtrl understands.
While push is on, TrueNAS alerts arrive by push, so the background check doesn\'t notify about them twice. Treat the push address like a password: anyone who has it can send you notifications.
